summary: assignments bulk-update sends the JSON list Canvas's bulk_update takes. --stdin unmarshalled into map[string]any, so the one endpoint whose body is a top-level array could not be called at all; the body is now checked for shape and passed through as the bytes that arrived. A body that is not a non-empty list of objects, and a run with no --stdin, are usage errors (exit 2) carrying a worked example, raised before any request. The generated local-mirror write is dropped: Canvas answers bulk_update with a Progress, not assignments. Short, Long, Example and the --stdin flag text are rewritten so the list is discoverable from --help.
reason:
Canvas's PUT /api/v1/courses/{id}/assignments/bulk_update is the only endpoint in this CLI whose request body is a JSON array. The generator writes one body shape for every write, map[string]any, so the command could reach Canvas only with an object body -- which Canvas answers with a queued job that then moves nothing. Date shifting a term is the agent's first job (JR-45, Plan E), and without a batch date edit it has to send one PUT per assignment, each a separate approval and a separate journal entry.

The bytes are passed through rather than re-marshalled from a Go value. The gateway reads the same array to decide which assignments to fetch a before-copy of (snapshot.BeforePaths via snapshotParams, which decodes the top-level array under "_json" as Rails names it), so the ids in it are what the undo record is built from. A round trip through map[string]any turns every number into a float64 and re-orders keys; nothing in the CLI needs to read this body, so nothing in the CLI should rewrite it. json.RawMessage also keeps the Content-Type on application/json, which the gateway requires before it will read the array at all (policy.IsJSON in journal.go).

Shape is checked before the request, not after Canvas rejects it: a list that is really an object is the mistake an agent that has been writing single-assignment updates actually makes, and the message hands back a working example. A run without --stdin is the same error, because --stdin is the only way to supply a list and the generated default was an empty object.

The mirror write had to go. bulk_update answers with a Progress -- {"id":1001,"workflow_state":"queued","tag":"assignment_bulk_update"} -- so writeMutationResponseToStore would upsert a job id into the assignments table and a later `--data-source local` read would serve an assignment 1001 that does not exist. The assignments are mirrored when they are read back.
known_limitations:
- Only the shape is checked. An entry's id is not looked up and all_dates is not validated, so a malformed date or an assignment in another course is Canvas's answer to give (and, inside Canvas Builder, the gateway's refusal).
- Write verification does not run on this command. verifyWrite compares the fields sent against the fields in the response and only accepts a map[string]any body, so a json.RawMessage list skips it. That is the right outcome rather than a gap: the response is a Progress and carries none of the fields sent, so a field-by-field comparison would call every bulk-update an ignored write. Reading the assignments back is the check, and the help text says so.
- The list is held in memory twice (the stdin bytes and the marshalled request body). A course's worth of assignment dates is tens of kilobytes, so this is not worth streaming.
- Canvas Builder refuses a list with more than 500 distinct assignment ids, because that is the cap on before-copies for one write (maxSnapshots in gateway journal.go), and the refusal it sends is the general 'Canvas Builder doesn't allow that' rather than anything about length. The help text tells the agent to batch a course that big; the wording is the gateway's to fix.
- Canvas's own partial behaviour is unchanged: bulk_update queues one job for the whole list, and a job that fails part-way through is reported by the Progress, not by this command's exit code.
- `bulk-update` is not in `which` yet; that is Task 11.
validated_outcome:
go build ./... clean. go test ./... passing across every package. go test -race -run BulkUpdate ./internal/cli/ clean. golangci-lint run on ./internal/cli/ reports nothing on any of the three files (the SA9003 'empty branch' findings on the other generated *_bulk_update.go files are pre-existing and untouched; the one in this file is gone because the dead branch now carries the refusal). gofmt clean on all three.

internal/cli/bulk_update_test.go:
- TestBulkUpdateSendsArray: the fake gateway receives exactly one PUT, Content-Type application/json, and a body byte-identical to the compacted list that went in on stdin, with ids 11 and 12 intact; Canvas's queued job reaches the agent in the envelope.
- TestBulkUpdateRefusesObject: seven bodies -- an object, an empty list, a list of numbers, a list holding a list, text that is not JSON, nothing at all, and a valid list with no --stdin -- each exit 2 carrying the example, with the fake gateway seeing zero requests.
- TestBulkUpdateDryRun: exit 0, zero requests, and the preview on stderr shows the method, the path and the list it would have sent; the envelope says dry_run true and success false.
- TestBulkUpdateDoesNotMirrorProgress: after a successful run the local mirror file was never created. Checked against itself by restoring the generated mirror write, which makes the test fail -- so the Progress really was being filed as an assignment.

Also confirmed by reading the gateway: undo_test.go uses the same Progress body for bulk_update, and snapshotParams requires a JSON content type before it will read the array.
